item.title: Trump: I spoke to Netanyahu, if we did anything in Iran, we'd hit Pickaxe
item.description:
US President Donald Trump told reporters he had spoken to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in recent days.
He then commented on the prospects of further strikes on Iran and said, “They haven't been able to do anything with their nuclear sites that we wiped out. But if we did anything, we would hit Pickaxe [Mountain]. I mean, we can tell them because they can't do anything about it."

item.title: Attack alerts issued in southwestern Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Saudi authorities issued attack alerts in the cities of Khamis Mushait and Abha in the southwestern part of the kingdom, near the border with Yemen.
The alerts were issued minutes after the Saudi-led coalition announced that it had intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Yemen's Houthi rebels toward southern Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Trump tells troops victory over Iran is at hand, questions Tehran's willingness to deal
item.description: In a Thanksgiving address to deployed US troops, Trump declares victory over Iran is within reach but questions whether Tehran will seize the chance for a deal.

item.title: Board of Peace official: We expect Israel to translate its commitments into action
item.description:
A Board of Peace official expressed encouragement over recent discussions with the Prime Minister's Office and Israel's commitment to US President Donald Trump's 20-point plan.
"The Board expects Israel to translate these words into action in the coming days," the official said, according to a report by Ynet.

item.title: Following attempted terror attack: Flydubai set to return to Israel
item.description: Israeli security officials approve a framework for Flydubai to resume flights to Israel. Flights could restart on December 3, subject to the airline's decision.

item.title: Security forces arrest suspect planning terrorist attack in central Israel
item.description: Yamam counterterrorism officers and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) personnel arrested a suspect in central Israel on Thursday evening after he expressed his intention to carry out a terrorist attack.

item.title: Rabbi Eliezer HaCohen Breuer, a longtime Temple Mount visitor, dies
item.description: Rabbi Eliezer HaCohen Breuer, a Soviet immigrant who championed Jewish settlement and holy sites, has died. For years, he took the first bus to the Temple Mount at 5 a.m. When daily trips became difficult, he decided to move to Jerusalem.

item.title: He said "Shema Yisrael" and feared the end: Yochai Badlov's rescue and recovery
item.description: Two and a half years after being critically wounded in Gaza, Yochai Badlov returns to yeshiva, recounts the miracles he experienced and dreams of starting a family.

item.title: Entrance to Ben Gurion Airport blocked by haredi protests
item.description: Surprise haredi demonstration blocks Ben Gurion Airport's Lod-Petah Tikva Gate in both directions. Flights operating as scheduled, without delays.

item.title: Heartbreaking Farewell: 'I'm sorry we didn't make more of every moment'
item.description: Two-year-old Liam Wein­stein was laid to rest Thursday at the Mishor Adumim cemetery, a day after he was killed in a suspected hit-and-run accident in Ma'ale Adumim.

item.title: Tzur Goldin: How Israel made kidnappings a strategic asset for Hamas
item.description: In a comprehensive study, Tzur Goldin, brother of the late Hadar Goldin, analyzes the failure of hostage policy before October 7, the impact of military pressure and how to prevent the next kidnapping.

item.title: Moti Shklar to Bennett: Your chance to truly repent and correct past mistakes
item.description: Media figure Moti Shklar urges Bennett to truly repent and pass the test he previously failed, voices dismay at promises to haredim and warns that forming a narrow government and deepening divisions pose an existential threat to Israel.

item.title: Mansour Abbas issues ultimatum to Eisenkot: "We will not sit idly by"
item.description: Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas told opposition bloc leaders his party would not abstain in a vote to form a government. He said Ra'am would support an Eisenkot-led government only if its demands were met; otherwise, it would vote against it.

item.title: Muslim slaughterhouse closed after animal abuse allegations
item.description: Florida authorities have shut down Ali Meat International, an Orlando-area slaughterhouse, following an extensive investigation into allegations of extreme animal cruelty.
